coverage_claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of the generic Service Case / Ticket aggregate across ISO guidance, Microsoft case-management documentation, Atlassian and Zendesk APIs, W3C provenance and IETF time standards, without a claim of universal sector, jurisdiction or platform completeness.

boundary_decision.rationale: The record-plane label standalone-mm is separate from subject kind. A service case groups intake, evolving decisions, role bindings, communications, evidence references, commitments and outcomes under one governed identity, so aggregate is more defensible than entity or event.

decisions.rationale: Request, inquiry, issue and complaint are represented as profile-bound case classifications. The base model does not force complaint-specific or vendor-specific semantics on every case.
The case handles a need or reported condition but references the originating incident, problem, product, service or asset, which retains independent identity and lifecycle.
Case assignment and coordination are native, while tasks, work orders and workflows remain independently governed and are linked by reference.
These roles can belong to different identities and have different authority, privacy and communication consequences, so they cannot be collapsed into one customer field.
Platform and organization vocabularies are not semantically identical. Every case pins the applicable profile and preserves original external codes during federation.

decisions.disposition: accepted as binding and observed instance only
decisions.rationale: The case records which entitlement, policy, KPI and calendar were applied and the resulting target, pause and breach observations, while policy design and time calculation remain external.
A resolved status does not prove requester acceptance, factual correction, regulatory compliance or completed downstream work. Each assertion retains its own authority and evidence.
The case owns chronology, relevance and visibility bindings while message, document, evidence and knowledge systems retain payload mastership and lifecycle.

decisions.disposition: not applicable to the case aggregate
decisions.rationale: A service case is an abstract aggregate. Physical properties belong to referenced affected objects, while case-local descriptive, temporal, relational and outcome properties remain native.
Append-only revisions, authority, ETag or equivalent concurrency, pinned mappings and explicit transform loss are required because cases are mutable and commonly synchronized across systems.

Every finding asks for current governed value, source and temporal provenance, and authorized revision or conflict handling. Repeated structure is machine-friendly but still needs later sector-profile editorial review.

publication_holds: Claude and Grok timed out during their bounded attempts, so independent external review is absent and explicitly waived for this published reviewable draft.
The shared relation ledger contains no approved outgoing edges for WM-ACT-021, so all sibling-model links in this draft are provisional composition proposals until registry reconciliation.

Clause and field-level mappings, exact external schema versions and round-trip behavior remain unverified for canonical conformance even though official source pages were checked during Codex research.
Sector and jurisdiction profiles must validate case types, status vocabularies, service commitments, closure, privacy and retention rules before operational enforcement.
deferred_research: Validate the logical structure against public service, healthcare, finance, education, legal, employment, facilities, IT service management and customer-support case profiles.
Create clause and field-level crosswalks for ISO 10002, Jira, Zendesk, Dynamics 365 and additional portable case-management schemas.
Approve sibling model identifiers, relation directions and cardinality contracts for parties, products, services, communications, evidence, work, policies, calendars and knowledge.
Review generated question wording with case workers, service agents, records managers, privacy officers and platform architects.
